newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says no need to sell insurer stock.
newsitem.headline: Merita says no need to sell insurer stock.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said on Friday it had no need to sell its shares in insurers Sampo or Pohjola to boost its capital adequacy ratio.

"We definitely have no need to boost capital adequacy further by disposing of those assets," Timo Nikinmaa, head of press relations, told Reuters by telephone. "There is certainly no reason to sell -- we couldn't use the extra capital adequacy even if we had it."

He was asked to comment on market talk that Merita may be seeking to sell its large holdings in the insurers. He said he understood the reason most frequently given in the market for such a plan would be for Merita to boost its capital adequacy.
"As far as I know we are not selling," he said. Nikinmaa said Merita holds 18.5 percent in Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola, and 15.9 percent -- held by a pension fund -- in Vakuutusosakeyhtio Sampo.

But he said the loan market in Finland is not improving fast enough to merit an increase in Merita's capital adequacy; and even if Merita did want to boost this it had scope to do so by issuing tier two capital.
He said Merita's group capital adequacy ratio at end-June was 10.9 percent, which theoretically could be boosted to about 12 percent.

The supposed motive behind a sale of the assets would be linked to Finnish legislation aimed at preventing double-gearing by banks and insurers, which means Merita must deduct large equity holdings in insurers when calculating capital adequacy.

The book value of Merita's Sampo holding at end-June was 865 million markka, compared to a market value of 756 million that day, and the book value of the Pohjola holding was 497 million markka against a market value then of 507 million, he said.
With Sampo trading around 326 markka at midday on Friday, the market value of Merita's holding would be about 916 million markka, slightly over its June book value.
Its stake in Pohjola, whose A and B series shares traded around 93 markka, would be worth around 602 million or well above its June book value.

Both Pohjola and Sampo rose sharply in Helsinki on revived rumours Merita was looking to sell the stakes, possibly to another Nordic insurer. Sweden's Skandia on Friday said it was not discussing a merger with Pohjola.
